summary: This study compares two fabricated electrodes: chitosan-derived porous carbon microspheres (CPCM) and the Ti3C2Tx-containing CPCM/MXene composite. Ti3C2Tx was prepared by LiF/HCl etching, then combined with hydrothermal chitosan spheres before KOH activation and carbonization to form a sandwich-like composite. The headline CPCM/MXene electrode delivered 362 F/g at 0.5 A/g in 1 mol/L H2SO4 in a three-electrode system; it also delivered 194.5 F/g at 1 A/g in a symmetric device using 1 mol/L Na2SO4. Numerical CPCM capacitance, mass loading, thickness, pore diameter, and interlayer-spacing values were not printed in the supplied paper text.
